## A live Plotly figure

This figure is generated by Python during the Quarto build and remains
interactive after static deployment.

::: {.chart-frame role="group" aria-label="Interactive line chart with x values 1 through 6 and y values 1.2, 2.8, 2.2, 4.6, 4.1, and 6.3"}
```{python}
import plotly.graph_objects as go
from IPython.display import HTML, display

fig = go.Figure(
    go.Scatter(
        x=[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6],
        y=[1.2, 2.8, 2.2, 4.6, 4.1, 6.3],
        mode="lines+markers",
        line={"color": "#087f8c", "width": 4},
        marker={"color": "#b84a2b", "size": 13},
        hovertemplate="step %{x}<br>signal %{y}<extra></extra>",
    )
)
fig.update_layout(
    template="plotly_white",
    height=470,
    margin={"l": 55, "r": 25, "t": 25, "b": 50},
    font={"color": "#172a33", "size": 17},
    xaxis_title="interaction",
    yaxis_title="insight",
    showlegend=False,
)
display(
    HTML(
        fig.to_html(
            full_html=False,
            include_plotlyjs="cdn",
            include_mathjax=False,
            config={"displayModeBar": False, "responsive": True},
        )
    )
)
```
:::

## Extend this deck

1. Add deterministic examples directly to this `.qmd` source.
2. Add Python packages with `uv add --project SLIDES package-name`.
3. Keep file-writing and cloud-publication calls out of renderable cells.
4. Treat Dash as linked source or a separately deployed application.

> Interactive Plotly figures are static-site compatible; Python callbacks are not.
